product_type: Rear combination lamp: an exterior lighting and signalling module combining rear position, stop and reversing lamps, an outer lens and a retro-reflector in one housing
summary: An LED rear combination lamp for an M1 passenger car. The specification states five elements: rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp, outer lens and retro-reflector. The attached two-view drawing is unscaled and unlabelled. It shows the internal module with the lens removed and the closed lens. The internal view shows an array of 24 reflector cups (3 rows of 8), a row of 8 small circular elements, an elongated upper channel, an empty rectangular compartment, and a lower-right compartment with a faceted curved reflector. The lens view shows a textured rectangular area at the lower right. The specification does not say which compartment carries which function. The spec describes the lens as red-tinted, yet a reversing lamp must emit white light, so the lens colour zoning needs confirmation. Materials are representative values only and must be confirmed against the bill of materials.

questions.question: Which compartment carries each function, and are any additional functions (rear direction indicator, rear fog lamp, end-outline marker) integrated?
questions.why_it_matters: Each extra function brings its own photometric, colour and installation requirements under UN R148/R48 and changes the approval marking.

questions.question: Is the light source a non-replaceable LED module, a replaceable LED light source, or a filament lamp per R37/R128?
questions.why_it_matters: This determines whether light-source approval under R37/R128 or light-source-module provisions apply, and how failure provisions are handled.

questions.question: Does the lamp contain active electronics (LED driver, ECU, failure-detection circuitry)?
questions.why_it_matters: Electronic sub-assemblies may need UN R10 EMC approval, and failure-mode requirements of R48/R148 may apply.

questions.question: Are the position and stop lamps reciprocally incorporated, and do they use variable intensity (R2/S2)?
questions.why_it_matters: This changes the R148 category marking, the test conditions, and the installation provisions.

questions.question: What is the retro-reflector class (e.g. IA, IB) and is it non-triangular red?
questions.why_it_matters: This determines the applicable R150 class requirements and whether separate retro-reflector approval or marking is needed.

questions.question: Is the lamp split across a movable component such as the tailgate or boot lid?
questions.why_it_matters: R48 imposes specific provisions on lamps mounted on movable components, including geometric visibility with the component open.

questions.question: How is the white reversing-lamp zone achieved given the red-tinted lens in the spec?
questions.why_it_matters: Colorimetric compliance for the reversing lamp (white) and the red functions must each be demonstrated separately under R148.

questions.question: What are the mounting height, lateral position and apparent surface on the target M1 vehicle?
questions.why_it_matters: These determine compliance with the R48 installation requirements for each function.
